evidence:
Scope per workbook Quality Checks #47: 'Shared pinned judge agent + model, pinned judge CLIs and browser, graded time rules on a fixed clock. Temperature and prompt-version markers are not required. Network is public here, so an open verifier network / missing allowlist is NOT a defect.' The Internal sheet's older wording ('temperature 0, versioned prompt ... no unpinned network in the scoring path') is superseded by that shipped wording and by SKILL.md 'Delivery profile'; I applied the shipped wording and skill section 47.

(1) Judge agent + model pinned and shared. task/task.toml [verifier.env] reads exactly 'REWARDKIT_JUDGE = "claude-code"', 'REWARDKIT_MODEL = "z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx"', 'ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL = "https://openrouter.ai/api"', 'ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN = "${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}"', 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = ""', identical to the frozen block in references/staged-task-contract.md; diff of task.toml against the template shows only name/description/keywords/difficulty/category/provenance/arena_slice changed. All five judge.toml [judge] blocks carry only judge = "claude-code", mode, timeout, isolated, prompt_template and mcp_servers; the documented grep for model|reasoning_effort|temperature in [judge] returns nothing. test.sh:63-66 refuses to grade if REWARDKIT_JUDGE/REWARDKIT_MODEL are unset, so no silent default model can be used.

(2) Judge CLIs, RewardKit and browser pinned. task/tests/Dockerfile:16-22 'npm install -g ... @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.281 @openai/codex@0.151.0 @playwright/mcp@0.0.79 express@5.1.0 better-sqlite3@12.4.1'; line 31 'pip3 install --no-cache-dir harbor-rewardkit==0.1.7'; lines 33-38 install chromium with the Playwright CLI that ships inside the pinned @playwright/mcp, so the browser build follows that pin, and every judge.toml launches it by fixed path ('--executable-path=/usr/local/bin/chromium'). Bases are tag-pinned ('FROM node:22-bookworm-slim', 'FROM python:3.12-slim'). test.sh contains no npx/npm/pip/curl/wget, so nothing is fetched or resolved at grade time by the harness.

(3) Shared files are the canonical ones. diff reports tests/Dockerfile, tests/test.sh, tests/scoring.toml, tests/tools/score.py, tests/tools/restart_mcp.py, tests/.dockerignore and environment/Dockerfile byte-identical to the frozen template under rules/projects/webdev-task-template.

(4) Graded time rules. No criterion, prompt or public note depends on the calendar date or wall-clock time: a grep for clock/date/timestamp/today across the task finds only test.sh:178 (a restart log stamp, not graded) and the golden's server.js created_at = new Date().toISOString() (lines 71, 84, 111), which no criterion reads; app_context.md names no clock. Every time-related criterion is a relative duration measured from the judge's own action with stated margin, e.g. cw_time_limit_recovery 'within about ten seconds a visible time-limit reason must appear ... Give the five-second budget normal scheduling margin and do not demand sub-second precision', cw_live_library_update 'watch its library for up to ten seconds', cw_stop_cancels_pending_work 'Then wait at least eight more seconds' with an explicit void-and-repeat rule if Stop is pressed late. So the 'fixed clock rather than the run date' requirement has nothing to bind to and is satisfied vacuously; grading the same app on a different day changes no expected value.

Counter-checks tried: a broken app cannot gain from the run date (no date-derived expected value exists); a conforming alternative that stores or shows revision times in any format or timezone is not penalised (no criterion reads them).

Notes (not defects in this row):
- N1: base images are pinned by tag, not digest, and apt packages plus 'install --with-deps chromium' system libraries are unversioned. This is the template's own text and the workbook treats 'unpinned apt' as a NOTE (check-dockerfiles.py).
- N2: the judge model is reached through OpenRouter with no provider/snapshot pin and no temperature; run-to-run judge variance is therefore possible. The row explicitly does not require temperature, and the block is frozen shared policy.
- N3: cw preview-isolation criterion (functional/judge.toml line 326) says 'If a public https address of your choice loads in a normal tab, repeat the no-cors fetch ... against it', so that sub-step depends on live public network and a judge-chosen host. It is conditional ('If ... loads') and the row says an open verifier network is not a defect; recorded only as a variance source.
- N4: several criteria rely on judge reaction time against 4-5 second windows (Stop 'as your very next action' before a four-second timer). The criteria carry controls and a void/repeat rule; whether the configured judge reliably meets them on these bytes is unmeasured and belongs to the tool-feasibility/workload rows.
- N5 (evidence hygiene): of the 22 hashes in raw-evidence-index.json, 18 match the files in cw-strict-worktree byte for byte. The four Oracle-run files (Rc3y2sT result.json, verifier/reward.json, verifier/scored/reward-details.json, verifier/gates/reward-details.json) hash differently on disk because that worktree checked them out with CRLF (core.autocrlf=true; 132/13/556/91 CR lines); with CRs removed, and as git index blobs, all four reproduce the indexed hashes exactly (4a9b1934..., bcfe3714..., bacbf94c..., 5b001eb8...). Content is intact; reward.json shows reward 0.9833 as indexed.
- N6: no configured judge run exists for these exact bytes (index scope says so). The hosted run on the earlier candidate shows the same pinned verifier stack launching and finishing (started 10:10:27Z, finished 10:52:12Z), which supports but does not measure these bytes. This row's own requirements are static and were verified from source, so I do not treat the gap as missing evidence for row 47.
